source_book: Sri Chaitanya — FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students, Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

conventions.matrix_notation: Matrices are written row-by-row as [[r1],[r2],…]; determinants are written det[[…]] or |[[…]]|.
conventions.transpose: The book prints the transpose as a superscript 1 (A¹) as often as A^T or A′. Every transpose is written Aᵀ in this index.
conventions.star_gutter: The scan is cropped at the inner gutter on several pages, which clips the ***/**/* prefix. Where a prefix may be clipped the recorded value is the MINIMUM legible count and notes say so; nothing is guessed upward.

questions.stem: Construct a 3 × 2 matrix whose elements are defined by aᵢⱼ = ½|i − 3j|.

questions.stem: If A = [[2, 4], [−1, k]] and A² = O, find the value of k.
If A = [[i, 0], [0, i]], find A².
If A = [[i, 0], [0, −i]], show that A² = −I.
If A = [[2, −4], [−5, 3]], find A + Aᵀ and AAᵀ.

Is [[0, 1, 4], [−1, 0, 7], [−4, −7, 0]] symmetric or skew-symmetric?
For any square matrix A, show that AAᵀ is symmetric.

questions.stem: A book shop holds 10 dozen chemistry books, 8 dozen physics books and 10 dozen economics books, selling at Rs. 80, Rs. 60 and Rs. 40 each respectively. Using matrix algebra, find the total value of the books in the shop.
questions.notes: The only word-problem in the chapter; it is also the only stem carrying a currency, so it needs a Rule-35 neutral restatement when authored.

questions.stem: Show that det[[a−b, b−c, c−a], [b−c, c−a, a−b], [c−a, a−b, b−c]] = 0.
If I = [[1, 0], [0, 1]] and E = [[0, 1], [0, 0]], show that (aI + bE)³ = a³I + 3a²bE.
If θ − φ = π/2, show that [[cos²θ, cos θ sin θ], [cos θ sin θ, sin²θ]] · [[cos²φ, cos φ sin φ], [cos φ sin φ, sin²φ]] = 0.

questions.stem: If A = [[1, −2, 3], [2, 3, −1], [−3, 1, 2]] and B = [[1, 0, 2], [0, 1, 2], [1, 2, 0]], check whether A and B commute under matrix multiplication.
questions.notes: The book words this as “verify A and B commute”; they do not, and the book's own conclusion is AB ≠ BA. Author it as a check, not as a “show that they commute”.

Prove that every square matrix can be expressed uniquely as the sum of a symmetric matrix and a skew-symmetric matrix.

questions.stem: Show that det[[a−b−c, 2a, 2a], [2b, b−c−a, 2b], [2c, 2c, c−a−b]] = (a + b + c)³.
Show that det[[a+b+2c, a, b], [c, b+c+2a, b], [c, a, c+a+2b]] = 2(a + b + c)³.
If det[[a, a², 1+a³], [b, b², 1+b³], [c, c², 1+c³]] = 0 and det[[a, a², 1], [b, b², 1], [c, c², 1]] ≠ 0, show that abc = −1.
Show that (det[[a, b, c], [b, c, a], [c, a, b]])² = det[[2bc−a², c², b²], [c², 2ac−b², a²], [b², a², 2ab−c²]] = (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc)².
Show that det[[b+c, c+a, a+b], [c+a, a+b, b+c], [a+b, b+c, c+a]] = 2·det[[a, b, c], [b, c, a], [c, a, b]].
Show that det[[1, a², a³], [1, b², b³], [1, c², c³]] = (a−b)(b−c)(c−a)(ab + bc + ca).

questions.notes: Q9's shared instruction is “Solve the following equations”; each of i)–vii) is a separate system. The three methods are three routes to one answer, so they are NOT split. Method sub-headers carry their own stars: *** matrix inversion, *** Cramer, *** Gauss-Jordan.

questions.stem: Solve x − y + 3z = 5, 4x + 2y − z = 0, −x + 3y + z = 5 by Cramer's rule, by matrix inversion and by the Gauss-Jordan method.
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT. The stem as printed gives the third equation as −x + 3y + 3z = 5, but every matrix the book then writes uses the row (−1, 3, 1), i.e. −x + 3y + z = 5, and only that version is consistent with the book's own Δ = 50 and answer (0, 1, 2). The corrected coefficient is used above. The Cramer's-rule restatement also mis-sets “x − y + 33 = 5” for x − y + 3z = 5.

questions.stem: Examine whether the system x + y + z = 3, 2x + 2y − z = 3, x + y − z = 1 is consistent or inconsistent, and if it is consistent find the complete solution.
